HxResult HxUiApplicationWindowResizes ( bool  resizeOnScreenChange  ) 

Set application window resizing behavior.

An application can call this function before calling HxUiInit to set the application's behavior with regards to screen dimension changes. The default behavior, equivalent to calling HxUiApplicationWindowResizes(false), is for the application window to stay at the LCD screen size.

After a call to HxUiApplicationWindowResizes(true), the application window will resize to match the size of the screen, which can change if the user has hooked up the device to a projector or monitor. Applications should listen for the kHxAppWindowResized message, or register a callback for the kHxPropertyScreenDimension notification to know when the window is resized.

This API should be called before your program's call to HxUiInit as it will affect the size of the application window created by HxUiInit. Changing this value after the program starts will not affect the system behavior.

Parameters:
resizeOnScreenChange IN: If set to true, application window resizes when the screen size changes; if false, the application window has a fixed size.
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success.

HxResult HxUiCustomFocusHandling ( bool  custom  ) 

Enable or disable focus handling.

HxUiCustomFocusHandling either enables or disables the default focus handling, or how the keyboard and/or scrollwheel is used to navigate from widget to widget. This API is provided for applications that need to customize how focus is implemented.

Note that HxUiCustomWheelHandling is used to customize scrollwheel events, while allowing the system to handle other events. HxUiCustomFocusHandling, however, disables all focus handling by the system.

When focus handling is customized, widgets are not added to the focus array when created. Instead, the application uses explicit calls to HxWidgetSetFocusArray at appropriate times to determine which widgets are included in the focus array.

The application is responsible for ensuring that HxWidgetSetFocusArray is called with the valid focusable widgets after a focusable widget is deallocated ro hidden. Failure to do this will lead to assertions on debug builds, and faults on release builds.

By default, focus handling is not customized, with the system adding all focusable widgets when they are allocated ro made visible, and removing them from the internal array when they are deallocated or hidden.

Parameters:
custom IN: If set to true, disable default focus handling
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK.

HxResult HxUiCustomWheelHandling ( HxKeyModifier_t  modifier  ) 

Customize scrollwheel handling.

HxUiCustomWheelHandling allows an application to override the default system behavior of how scrollwheel events affect focus handling.

The system has the following default behavior:

Scrollwheel with kHxKeyModifierNone: change the selection of a dropdown box or list that has focus, or scroll a container when the container has focus.

Scrollwheel with kHxKeyModifierShift: change widget focus backward or forward, depending on the direction the scrollwheel is moved.

The modifier argument is a bitmask, so more than one modifier can be customized. Only kHxKeyModifierNone, kHxKeyModifierShift, kHxKeyModifierAlt and kHxKeyModifierAltGr are used by the system, however.

Use kHxKeyModifierNotCustom to disable all scrollwheel customization. If other modifier flags are combined, they are ignored, and will no longer override default system behavior.

HX_INVALID_ARG is returned if bits other than kHxKeyModifierNone, kHxKeyModifierShift, kHxKeyModifierAlt, or kHxKeyModifierNotCustom are set.

Parameters:
modifier IN: Bitmask modifier key
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK.

HxResult HxUiExitEventLoopIfIdle ( bool  exitIfIdle  ) 

Set mode of event loop.

This function changes how events are processed by HxWindowEventLoop.

By default, HxWindowEventLoop exits when its timeout expires, or as a result of the deletion of the app window.

If the exitIfIdle argument of this function is set to true, HxWindowEventLoop exits prior to the expiration of the timeout if the event queue is empty.

If you find yourself wanting this function, you should look at using HxWindowSetIdleCallback instead, as that doesn't cause the event loop to exit, it just calls a helper function when it goes idle.

Parameters:
exitIfIdle IN: If set to true, exit when idle
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK.

HxResult HxUiFindLocaleDependentFile ( const char *  pDefaultDir,
const char *  pName,
char **  pFoundFile 
)

Return the file to be used for the given locale.

This returns a char* file path for a locale dependent file. This function takes the given file and tries to determine if the current locale requires a locale specific resource file to be used. If an alternate locale is currently being used and a locale specific resource file is present it will return the locale specific file. If not it will return the input file path. The user is responsible for using g_free to free pFoundFile.

Parameters:
pDefaultDir IN: The directory the requested file is in.
pName IN: The name of the requested file.
pFoundFile OUT: The locale specific file to use or the original request file is a locale specific one was not found. The user is responsible for using g_free to free this value.
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK

HxResult HxUiGetSystemBitmap ( HxUiSystemBitmap_t  name,
HxImageDescription_t **  hImage 
)

Return the HxImageDescription_t for a system bitmap.

This returns an HxImageDescription_t for a system bitmap that can be used by many applications. Images are cached by the system. When you are finished with the HxImageDescripton_t, you need to release it using a call to HxImageDescriptionDelete().

Parameters:
name IN: The selector for the system bitmap.
hImage OUT: HxImageDescription_t is returned here.
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if image was loaded. Returns HX_FAILURE if image type was not found.

HxResult HxUiGetWheelScalingFactor ( int32_t *  pScalingFactor  ) 

Return the scaling factor to apply to wheel movement.

This function stores the scaling factor that should be applied to wheel movement. Normally this is applied to scroll events that affect widgets like fields and other views that act like a viewport. For widgets where the wheel selects items, the scaling factor should not be applied.

The default value is 3, but this can be changed by editing /etc/hx/hxui.ini.

Parameters:
pScalingFactor OUT: pointer to an integer
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK.

HxResult HxUiSetApplicationWindowColor ( const HxColor_t *  pColor  ) 

Set application window background color.

An application can call this before calling HxUiInit to set the color that's used to draw the background of the application window. This can be used to minimize color flashing on application startup when the app isn't using the standard white background color. This function can also be used while the application is active to change the color of the application window; it will trigger a redraw of the app window and all of its child widgets.

Parameters:
pColor IN: pointer to window background color
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HK_OK on success.
